text:
Alex (sales): quick flag — demo for BetaRetail just hit a 413 during a live walkthrough. they sent a single POST with product images + descriptions.
Lina (solutions): oh no. do we know whether the 413 came from the edge or our app? what size?
Alex (sales): customer says ~7.5MB. curl returned "413 Request Entity Too Large". they were calling the hosted /v1/chat endpoint.
Raj (engineer): likely nginx body_limit on the demo route. default hosted demo limit is 5MB. can we get a sanitized request example?
Alex (sales): yup, sent in DM. gist: large JSON with base64-encoded PNGs embedded under items[].image.
Mei (oncall): short-term options: 1) bump tenant body_limit to 12MB for the scheduled demo window, 2) advise client to upload binary blobs separately (presign), 3) client compresses payload with gzip and sets Content-Encoding.
Lina (solutions): presign + reference URLs is best practice. but customer is doing an in-browser demo and wants one-call convenience. any client-side workaround?
Raj (engineer): can do client-side chunking: send only item metadata in first request, stream generation for each chunk, then stitch responses. or send small summary + fetch more via embedding lookups.
Lina (solutions): add to that: swap to an xlong model variant if they need >8k tokens for descriptions. that helps avoid truncation-related regressions.
Alex (sales): pricing / security questions — will presigning change Redwood billing or data residency?
Lina (solutions): billing unaffected (tokens billed as usual). storage/egress on customer's side. for residency: they can presign to their own S3 (VPC/backed) or we can support encrypted uploads to a presign endpoint that keeps blobs in their cloud account.
Mei (oncall): operationally I can approve a temporary body_limit bump for the tenant if we get a ticket with tenant id + window. prefer narrow window + monitoring.
Alex (sales): tenant beta-retail-9, window Mon 2026-03-23 16:00-16:30 UTC. putting in the ticket now.
ConfigBot: deploy request received: increase body_limit for tenant beta-retail-9 to 12MB between 2026-03-23T16:00:00Z and 2026-03-23T16:30:00Z. awaiting oncall approval.
Mei (oncall): approved. I'll annotate the change and watch logs.
Raj (engineer): also advise compression tip: base64 expands binary by ~33%. if they send raw binary (multipart/presign) or gzip before base64, payload shrinks a lot. include this quick snippet in the demo repo:
```
// client-side gzip example (node)
const zlib = require('zlib')
const payload = JSON.stringify(body)
const gz = zlib.gzipSync(payload)
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Encoding': 'gzip' }, body: gz })
```
Lina (solutions): I'll create a 1-page demo checklist: presign pattern, gzip header snippet, chunked streaming pattern, model variant guidance, and the exact step to request a short body_limit bump.
Alex (sales): customer asked if we can temporarily accept POSTs with base64 images for the demo only — is that acceptable?
Raj (engineer): acceptable for demo with a short window, but warn about increased latency and memory on the edge. recommend presign as follow-up.
ConfigBot: change applied: body_limit set to 12MB for tenant beta-retail-9. will auto-revert at 2026-03-23T16:30:00Z.
Alex (sales): confirmed demo ran. customer saw successful product ingest and generation. sending follow-up with the presign + gzip recommendations. :tada:
Lina (solutions): closing loop. I'll attach the checklist and a sample code patch to the support ticket.
Mei (oncall): logs looked clean during window. no error spikes. all good.
Alex (sales): thanks team!
